items.q: A 22-year-old motorcyclist sustains head trauma. Non-contrast CT reveals a high-attenuation biconvex lenticular extra-axial hematoma over the left temporoparietal convexity that does NOT cross the lambdoid or coronal suture lines. Which vessel is most likely lacerated?
items.exp: An epidural hematoma classical presents as a biconvex lenticular collection confined by cranial sutures, most commonly caused by skull fracture at the pterion lacerating the middle meningeal artery.
r: Correct. Middle meningeal artery rupture creates a high-pressure biconvex collection bounded by cranial sutures.
Incorrect. Bridging vein shearing produces a crescentic subdural hematoma that crosses suture lines.
Incorrect. Dural sinus tears are less common and typically associate with depressed skull fractures.
Incorrect. Anterior cerebral artery injury causes intracerebral or subarachnoid hemorrhage.
items.kp: Epidural hematomas arise from middle meningeal artery laceration, producing biconvex collections limited by cranial suture attachments.

items.q: During human neuroembryogenesis at 5 weeks of gestation, which secondary brain vesicle gives rise to the adult pons and cerebellum?
items.exp: The rhombencephalon (hindbrain) divides into the metencephalon (which develops into the pons and cerebellum) and the myelencephalon (which forms the medulla oblongata).
r: Correct. The metencephalon develops into the pons and cerebellum.
Incorrect. The myelencephalon develops into the adult medulla oblongata.
Incorrect. The mesencephalon persists as the adult midbrain.
Incorrect. The diencephalon develops into the thalamus and hypothalamus.
items.kp: Rhombencephalon subdivides into metencephalon (pons and cerebellum) and myelencephalon (medulla oblongata).

items.q: An 82-year-old patient with cerebral atrophy presents with progressive confusion and gait unsteadiness three weeks after a minor fall. Brain CT shows a crescent-shaped extra-axial collection along the cerebral convexity crossing the coronal suture line. What is the source of bleeding?
items.exp: Subdural hematomas result from rupture of delicate bridging cerebral veins spanning the subdural space, forming a crescent-shaped collection that freely crosses cranial suture lines.
r: Correct. Bridging veins tear easily in elderly patients with brain atrophy, producing crescentic subdural hematomas.
Incorrect. Middle meningeal artery produces biconvex epidural hematomas that do not cross sutures.
Incorrect. Internal carotid laceration is an arterial skull base trauma injury.
Incorrect. Aneurysm rupture causes subarachnoid hemorrhage.
items.kp: Subdural hematomas result from sheared bridging veins, creating crescent-shaped collections that cross cranial suture lines.

items.q: Due to the sharp 90-degree cephalic flexure of the human neuraxis, in which direction does the term 'rostral' refer when describing the cerebral hemispheres?
items.exp: Above the midbrain in the cerebrum, the cephalic flexure rotates the axis so that rostral corresponds to anterior (towards the frontal pole) and caudal corresponds to posterior.
r: Correct. In the cerebrum rostral means anterior towards the frontal pole.
Incorrect. In the cerebrum superior corresponds to dorsal.
Incorrect. Posterior corresponds to caudal in the cerebrum.
Incorrect. Inferior corresponds to ventral in the forebrain.
items.kp: At the cephalic flexure the neuraxis bends 90 degrees: in the cerebrum rostral means anterior and caudal means posterior.

items.q: The tentorium cerebelli represents a major reflection of which meningeal layer?
o: Inner meningeal layer of dura mater
items.exp: Dural reflections including the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli are formed by duplications of the inner meningeal layer of the cranial dura mater.
r: Correct. The meningeal layer of dura mater reflects to form intracranial septa including tentorium cerebelli.
Incorrect. Arachnoid mater lines the dura but does not form rigid dural folds.
Incorrect. Pia mater closely invests cerebral parenchyma.
Incorrect. Periosteal dura adheres to inner skull bones.
items.kp: Dural folds such as the tentorium cerebelli and falx cerebri are formed by the inner meningeal layer of dura mater.

items.q: Between which two anatomical layers does cerebrospinal fluid circulate around the brain and spinal cord?
items.exp: Cerebrospinal fluid circulates within the subarachnoid space, bounded externally by the arachnoid mater and internally by the pia mater.
r: Correct. The subarachnoid space lies between arachnoid mater and pia mater.
Incorrect. Space between dura and arachnoid is the subdural plane.
Incorrect. Space between skull and dura is the epidural space.
Incorrect. The glial limitans underlies the closely adherent pia mater.
items.kp: Cerebrospinal fluid circulates within the subarachnoid space between arachnoid and pia mater.

items.q: Which adult brain structure is embryologically derived directly from the diencephalon?
items.exp: The diencephalon develops into the thalamus, hypothalamus, epithalamus, and subthalamus, surrounding the third ventricle.
r: Correct. Thalamus and hypothalamus originate from the embryological diencephalon.
Incorrect. Cerebral cortex originates from the telencephalon.
Incorrect. Pons and cerebellum originate from the metencephalon.
Incorrect. Medulla oblongata originates from the myelencephalon.
items.kp: The diencephalon gives rise to the thalamus, hypothalamus, subthalamus, and epithalamus.

items.q: A fracture involving the pterion on the lateral calvarium is clinically critical because it overlies which vascular structure?
o: Anterior branch of middle meningeal artery
items.exp: The pterion is the junction of frontal, parietal, sphenoid, and temporal bones. Its thin bone directly overlies the anterior division of the middle meningeal artery.
r: Correct. The pterion overlies the anterior division of the middle meningeal artery.
Incorrect. Internal carotid siphon lies deep in the cavernous sinus.
Incorrect. Transverse sinus runs posteriorly at the occipitotemporal junction.
Incorrect. Middle cerebral artery runs deep in the lateral Sylvian sulcus.
items.kp: Pterion fractures frequently tear the underlying anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery, precipitating epidural hematoma.

items.q: Herniation of the medial temporal lobe uncus through the tentorial notch compresses which cranial nerve first, causing an ipsilateral dilated non-reactive pupil?
items.exp: Uncal herniation pushes the uncus across the tentorial edge, compressing the ipsilateral oculomotor nerve (CN III). The superficial parasympathetic pupilloconstrictor fibers are damaged first, yielding an ipsilateral blown pupil.
r: Correct. CN III is compressed against the petroclinoid ligament by the herniating uncus.
Incorrect. CN IV has the longest intracranial course but is less immediately compressed by uncal mass effect.
Incorrect. CN VI is vulnerable to downward traction from elevated intracranial pressure.
Incorrect. Trigeminal nerve lies in Meckel cave.
items.kp: Uncal herniation compresses the ipsilateral oculomotor nerve, leading to ipsilateral pupillary dilation and sluggish light reflex.

items.q: Lumbar puncture safely accesses the subarachnoid space at the L3-L4 or L4-L5 intervertebral space because in adults the conus medullaris terminates at which vertebral level?
items.exp: In the adult human, the spinal cord terminates as the conus medullaris at the L1-L2 vertebral interspace. A lumbar puncture at L3-L4 enters the lumbar cistern without risking spinal cord puncture.
r: Correct. Adult spinal cord ends at L1-L2; lumbar puncture at L3-L4 or L4-L5 safely samples cerebrospinal fluid.
Incorrect. L4-L5 is where the needle is placed, well below the cord termination.
Incorrect. T10-T11 contains active spinal cord segments.
Incorrect. S1-S2 marks the lower end of the dural sac.
items.kp: The conus medullaris terminates at L1-L2 in adults, allowing safe lumbar puncture access at L3-L4 or L4-L5.
